metadata.title: THE ROLE OF SUBNATIONAL GOVERNMENTS IN ADULT SKILLS SYSTEMS: KOREA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is a governance and responsibilities mapping for Korea’s adult skills system, not an analysis of student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC). As such, there is no sampling frame for students, no plausible values (PV) generation, and no survey-weight variables to apply. The document describes institutional roles and expenditure shares at subnational levels (e.g., % of general government expenditure at the sub-national level) using compiled secondary information rather than a weighted statistical estimation. Therefore, complex survey design weights and replicate weights are not applicable to the reported content.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document does not conduct an empirical student-level assessment analysis and does not use PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. Instead, it provides a descriptive overview of governance structures, stakeholder responsibilities, and expenditure allocation across national, regional, and local levels. Because there is no PV-based outcome modeling, missing-data handling for PVs or student responses is not part of the study design.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used a secondary-information compilation to describe Korea’s adult skills governance structure and subnational expenditure shares; no analytic student sample or inclusion/exclusion criteria are defined.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Korea country note synthesizes governance arrangements for adult skills systems across levels of government (national, regional, and local) and across policy areas (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery). It characterizes Korea as a relatively decentralised system where most implementation and funding allocation occurs at regional and local levels, and it reports the subnational share of general government expenditure (45.8%). The note also details which ministries and agencies oversee ALMPs versus education and training policy areas (VET/HVET/CET/AE), and it maps responsibilities to stakeholders such as employment centres, lifelong learning institutions, and regional/local education authorities. Because the document is descriptive and based on compiled secondary sources rather than student assessment microdata, it does not estimate model-based performance metrics or ML predictions, and no PV or missing-data procedures are applicable.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the document is a governance/implementation overview rather than an empirical large-scale assessment study. There is no student-level dataset, no assessment cycle, and no statistical modeling of outcomes; consequently, fields such as sample size, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not populated. This is consistent with a descriptive policy note that maps institutional responsibilities and expenditure structure using secondary references.
